title.es: Una historia que vale la pena repetir

es: Construir y contar una historia con gancho, conflicto, resolución y una idea final, y responder a dos preguntas de un oyente.

teaching.en: A story people want to retell starts with a hook: 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'
teaching.es: Una historia que la gente quiere volver a contar empieza con un gancho: «Me subí al tren equivocado y lo cambió todo».
teaching.explanationEs: Retell = contar de nuevo; el gancho despierta curiosidad en la primera frase.
segments: A story people want to retell starts with a hook:
'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'
teaching.audioText: A story people want to retell starts with a hook: 'I got on the wrong train, and it changed everything.'

teaching.en: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the train was heading for a city I did not know.
teaching.es: El conflicto es el problema que el personaje no puede ignorar: el tren iba hacia una ciudad que yo no conocía.
segments: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the
train was heading for a city I did not know.
teaching.audioText: The conflict is the problem the character cannot ignore: the train was heading for a city I did not know.

teaching.en: The resolution shows how the problem ended: 'A stranger shared her map, and I found my way.'
teaching.es: La resolución muestra cómo terminó el problema: «Una desconocida compartió su mapa y encontré mi camino».
segments: The resolution shows how the problem ended: 'A stranger
shared her map, and I found my way.'
teaching.audioText: The resolution shows how the problem ended: 'A stranger shared her map, and I found my way.'

teaching.en: Add one vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, so the listener can see the scene.
teaching.es: Añade un detalle vívido, como el olor a naranjas en el andén, para que el oyente vea la escena.
teaching.explanationEs: Un solo detalle vivid vale más que cinco generales.
segments: Add one vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges
on the platform, so the listener can see the scene.
teaching.audioText: Add one vivid detail, such as the smell of oranges on the platform, so the listener can see the scene.

teaching.en: End with a takeaway: 'Sometimes the wrong train takes you to the right place.'
teaching.es: Termina con una idea final: «A veces el tren equivocado te lleva al lugar correcto».
teaching.explanationEs: Takeaway es lo que el oyente se lleva y repetirá.
segments: End with a takeaway: 'Sometimes the wrong
train takes you to the right place.'

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase funciona mejor como gancho de una historia de viaje?

choices.text: I want to tell you about a trip.
I got on the wrong train, and it changed my life.
This story is about a train journey.

feedback.es: Despierta curiosidad con un hecho concreto y una promesa de cambio; las otras solo anuncian el tema.

hint.es: Busca la frase que despierta curiosidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una historia termina con una idea final que el oyente puede llevarse.»

feedback.es: Takeaway es la idea que el oyente se lleva y puede repetir.

hint.es: Es lo que se «lleva» el oyente.

origin.text: A story ends with a ___: one idea the listener can take away.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un desconocido me dio su mapa.»

answer.text: A stranger gave me his map

feedback.es: Sujeto, verbo, persona y objeto: «gave me his map».

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es el conflicto de esta historia?

choices.text: They had planned a perfect picnic.
A farmer drove them home.
The path flooded and they could not find the car.

feedback.es: El conflicto es el problema central: el camino inundado y el coche perdido.

origin.text: We had planned a perfect picnic. Then the rain started, the path flooded, and we could not find the car. A farmer drove us home in his car.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la resolución de la historia.

choices.text: She found her brother laughing beside a musician.
She called the police about the festival.
Her brother never came back.

feedback.es: Lo encuentra riendo junto a un músico: así termina el problema.

origin.audio: When I was twelve, I lost my little brother at a festival. For ten terrible minutes, I searched every stall. Then I heard him laughing. He was sitting beside a musician. Since then, I never let go of his hand.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la pieza de la historia que representa.

pairs: Forty years ago, my uncle sold his car and bought a boat.
The boat leaked on the first day, and there was no land anywhere.
He pressed his shirt against the leak and reached the island at dawn.
A small problem is just a story you have not finished yet.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: abre con curiosidad, plantea el problema, lo resuelve y deja una idea.

pairs: Forty years ago, my uncle sold his car and bought a boat.
The boat leaked on the first day, and there was no land anywhere.
He pressed his shirt against the leak and reached the island at dawn.
A small problem is just a story you have not finished yet.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito se cuenta esta historia breve?

choices.text: To inspire listeners with a great success
To warn listeners about a costly mistake
To persuade listeners to buy a bike

feedback.es: Muestra un error (no cerrar la bici), su coste y una petición final: advierte.

origin.text: I never locked my bike. Last winter, someone took it from outside my door. Please lock yours today.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la frase que resume la reflexión final.

choices.text: The neighbours were always friendly.
The roof was sold.
The problem led them to a better option.

feedback.es: Tras «Looking back» concluye que el muro los empujó a algo mejor.

origin.audio: We used to eat on the roof every evening. Then, suddenly, the neighbours built a wall in front of it. I was furious at first, but eventually we started to use the garden. Looking back, the wall made us find something better.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes vivía en Quito, pero ahora vivo junto al mar.»

feedback.es: Vivir es un estado del pasado que ya no continúa: se usa used to, no would.

origin.text: I ___ live in Quito, but now I live by the sea.

prompt.es: Cuenta una historia familiar con gancho, conflicto, resolución e idea final.

answer.text: Fifty years ago, my grandmother missed the last bus the night before her wedding. She was alone on a dark road, and it started to rain. Then a farmer stopped and offered her a lift. She arrived at dawn, tired and muddy, but she reached the church on time. The lesson? Sometimes help comes from the people you least expect. Was she worried? Terribly, but she kept walking. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was standing at the church door, and they stayed together for fifty years.
accepted: Fifty years ago, my grandmother missed the last bus the night before her wedding. She was alone on a dark road, and it started to rain. Then a farmer stopped and offered her a lift. She arrived at dawn, tired and muddy, but she reached the church on time. The lesson? Sometimes help comes from the people you least expect. Was she worried? Terribly, but she kept walking. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was standing at the church door, and they stayed together for fifty years.

My grandmother always tells us about the night before her wedding. She missed the last bus, and she had to walk in the rain. Suddenly, a farmer stopped his car and gave her a lift, so she got home at dawn. Was she worried? Yes, but she kept calm. Did he wait for her? Of course! My grandfather was at the church door that same morning. The takeaway is simple: people can surprise you when you need them.

feedback.es: La historia tiene gancho, conflicto (perder el bus), resolución (el granjero), idea final y respuestas a las dos preguntas del oyente.

origin.text: Datos: tu abuela perdió el último autobús la noche antes de su boda; un granjero la llevó en su coche; llegó al amanecer, cansada y con barro. Un oyente pregunta: «Was she worried?» y «Did he wait for her?». Responde a ambas dentro del texto y cierra con una idea final.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase deja claro lo que está en juego?

choices.text: If he missed the ferry, he would lose his job.
We used to work in a big office.
The ferry arrived on Monday.

feedback.es: Combina la amenaza con un condicional: si falla, pierde algo concreto.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué efecto crea esta secuencia de marcadores.

choices.text: A sudden shock with a quick ending
A slow loss of contact that builds suspense
A funny story with a joke

feedback.es: «Gradually» y «eventually» muestran una pérdida lenta que aumenta la tensión.

origin.audio: At first, nothing seemed unusual. Gradually, the phone rang less often. Eventually, it stopped ringing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mirando atrás, fue lo mejor que me pasó.»

answer.text: Looking back it was the best thing that happened to me

feedback.es: La reflexión abre con «Looking back» y usa «that» tras «thing».
